meta.title: AI Workflow Case Study — Billy Pronovost
meta.description: A public, sanitized case study on AI-assisted technology operations reporting and the Lumi/Hermes latest experiment.

hero.kicker: AI WORKFLOW CASE STUDY / CURRENT ROLE
hero.title: AI-assisted reporting with human approval.
hero.statement: A weekly Technology Operations reporting workflow turns scattered operational inputs into a leadership-ready draft, while I verify the evidence, priorities, and final voice before anything is shared.

workflow.label: Source
workflow.title: Collect the operating picture
workflow.body: Team recap submissions, meeting notes, Work Radar items, a prior finalized report, and live Jira queries are gathered as the source set.

workflow.label: Structure
workflow.title: Ask AI to shape the draft
workflow.body: The assistant organizes the source material into reporting sections, carries forward open priorities, and highlights gaps instead of inventing answers.

workflow.label: Review
workflow.title: Verify before it leaves the room
workflow.body: I check source completeness, Jira counts, status and priority changes, tone, omissions, and whether each claim is safe to share.

workflow.label: Publish
workflow.title: Approve the leadership version
workflow.body: Only the reviewed and finalized report becomes the record. AI accelerates synthesis; accountability stays human.

ai: Structures a first draft from known inputs
Carries forward priorities from prior reports
Surfaces missing or ambiguous source areas
human: Checks Jira counts and status changes
Approves the final report and owns the decision

guardrails.title: No sensitive identifiers
guardrails.body: The public case study avoids confidential project names, ticket keys, team names, screenshots, source data, credentials, internal systems, and private memory contents.

guardrails.title: Evidence stays inspectable
guardrails.body: The workflow treats source completeness and query results as checks, not assumptions.

guardrails.title: AI cannot finalize
guardrails.body: Drafting and synthesis are delegated. Approval, business judgment, and communication responsibility are not.

experiment.title: Latest experiment: Lumi / Hermes
experiment.body: Lumi/Hermes is a persistent AI partner runtime I use for real work. It can load context, invoke tools, edit files, run scheduled tasks, and verify outputs. The experiment is not replacing judgment; it is making the path from intent to tested artifact shorter.

answer: Today I use AI as part of a weekly Technology Operations reporting workflow. It brings together team recaps, meeting notes, open work, the prior finalized report, and live Jira data. AI helps organize the inputs, identify gaps, carry forward open priorities, and produce a leadership-ready draft. I remain responsible for accuracy and final judgment: I verify source coverage, Jira counts, status and priority changes, tone, omissions, and every claim before anything is shared. My latest experiment is Lumi/Hermes, a persistent AI partner runtime I built and continue to develop. It maintains context across work, uses tools, edits real files, runs scheduled workflows, and verifies outputs while keeping decisions and approval with me. The attached case study shows how I use that system in practice, including what the AI handles, where human review remains required, and the controls that keep the result grounded. A visual walkthrough is available at wdpronovost.com/ai-workflow/.
